recipes.name: Campbell's Swiss Vegetable Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (Regular, 98% Fat Free or 25% Less Sodium)
1 (16 ounce) bag frozen vegetable combination (broccoli, cauliflower, carrots), thawed

steps.text: Stir soup, sour cream, black pepper, vegetables, 2/3 cup onions and 1/4 cup cheese in 2-quart casserole. Cover casserole.
Bake at 350 degrees F 40 minutes or until vegetables are tender. Stir vegetable mixture.
Top with remaining onions and cheese. Bake 5 minutes or until cheese is melted.

raw_recipe.headline: Campbell's Swiss Vegetable Casserole
raw_recipe.description: A colorful vegetable combination is mixed with Campbell's Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup, Swiss cheese and sour cream, then topped with French fried onions and more Swiss cheese, and baked until golden and bubbly.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe for years. I don't put in the sour cream or the pepper, since I don't like pepper and I wanted to cut down on the fat content. I also don't put in the cheese for the same reason. It's very good without all that and everyone I've served it to has liked it.

This is my go to holiday side dish or group gathering recipe. It replaces the more traditional green bean casserole for our family because I have a few folks that don't like green beans or mushrooms. So here are my changes and substitutions: 
I double the recipe, which fits nicely in a medium aluminum casserole dish. I put the veggies in frozen and cook the whole thing for an extra half hour (1 hour to cook and an extra 10 after you add the cheese and onion topping)
I substitute cream of celery soup for the cream of mushroom (I have mushroom haters in the family). 
I add a total of 1 1/2 cups cheese.

This is one of my favorite vegetable casseroles. I changed it by adding a cup of sour cream instead of just 1/3 cups, and change the cheese from swiss to sharp cheddar. I also add frozen corn thawed. I love cheese so I mix 1 1/2 cups of sharp cheddar into the casserole while it is baking and then top with the last 1/2 cup and remaining onions. Very good. If you want to make a whole meal out of this, you can add a can of mushrooms to the mixture, 1/4 cup of milk and then add 4 chicken breasts that you have cooked partially in the skillet and then place in a bottom of a 9X13 pan and cover with the vegetable casserole. The chicken stays moist and it is a nice combination of flavors.
Always looking for a new spin on Mac-N-Cheese, so I added 1 cup cooked pasta and 12 ounces cooked broccoli. Then topped it off with 2 sliced Roma tomatoes and then the crushed onion rings. Oh-la-la!

I used 48oz of the California mix vegetables, a 26oz can of Cream of Mushroom soup (tried to get low sodium, but could not find it), and substituted plain Greek yogurt for the sour cream. I increased the amount of yogurt and cheese roughly in proportion to the extra soup and veggies. Also, used a 6oz can of the French Fried Onions. 
The veggies weren't completely thawed, so I set the oven to 375, and cooked a maybe 10 minutes longer (sorry, I'm a bad scientist in the kitchen - I go with instinct a lot).
There wasn't much leftover, and what was left was taken home by other guests. I was told it was in fact "a hit".
I'll do it again, and experiment with reducing the overall sodium and fat content, and maybe incorporating other vegetables.

Made a whole bunch of substitutions because this was a last minute recipe I made to use up a bag of frozen carrots and beans that was languishing in my freezer. I used 1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt instead of the sour cream and added two cans of canned skinless-boneless canned salmon to provide protein. I didn’t have any fried onions so I topped it with Panko crumbs and used cheddar cheese where the recipe called for Swiss. Still turned out totally delicious!
yes i will make it again i used fresh brocoli and cauliflower and carrots

I have been making this for years, and it is always a hit with company.
In order to keep the calorie count down I use low fat sour cream, reduced fat swiss cheese, and Campbell's Healthy Request Cream of Mushroom soup. It's delicious~

I've been making this recipe for years and always serve it as a side to Chicken Parisian Crepes that I make. I love the addition of the sour cream to make it richer. For those who do not like swiss cheese, I've made it with muenster, but swiss is my favorite. To make things cook more quickly (and avoid crunchy vegetables), I often pre-cook the veggies in the microwave with a little water to speed things up. This is always a hit!

I made the sauce, but did not have any broccoli. Instead I used cauliflower, carrots, zucchini, and celery. I diced the vegetables and steamed them just to ala dente. I folded them into the sauce which I had cooked on top of the stove until the cheese was melted. Some black pepper and the dish was done. This was simple and delicious. I will definitely make it again.

I have made this for years. We always have it with ham for Christmas dinner. Everyone loves it...even the kids who don't normally like veggies. We use cream of celery soup instead of mushroom. I usually have to double or triple the recipe because everyone likes it so much.
Humongous hit! My 16 year old, who is a true hater of veggies, absolutely loved it. It was very easy too! On my top 10 list.
My MIL makes this all the time, she adds pimento, I love it.

Absolutely love the swiss veggie casserole! This dish been part of our families thanksgiving tradition for years! No changes made to the ingredients, followed as recipe as described! Thank you Campbell’s! Happy Thanksgiving!
This is one of my favorite recipes of all times! But I use a whole cup of shredded Swiss instead of half so you can really taste the nutty-flavor of the Swiss.
Had this at friends house Thanksgiving, and I loved it. Making for my Christmas dinner. Remembered that it was bland so I add bacon. Should be so tasty.
Excellent, so tasty. I didn't have Swiss cheese so I used shredded Italian blend. I will definitely make this again. Quick and easy!
Yummy. Greatly way to get your vegetable intake.
